chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who arrived in Makkah with his sacrifice during the ten (days of Dhu al-Hijjah), he (peace be upon him) said: 'If his offering was obligatory, he should not slaughter it except in Mina; and if it was not obligatory, let him slaughter it in Makkah if he wishes; and if he had decorated it and yoked it, he should not slaughter it except on the Day of Sacrifice.'

key_terms.قَلَّدَهُ: Yoked or fitted with a neck-ring
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a location near Makkah where Eid prayers and sacrifices occur
key_terms.هَدْي: Sacrificial animal brought by a pilgrim for Hajj

ai.seo_question: Where and when should a pilgrim slaughter their Hajj sacrifice depending on whether it is obligatory or voluntary?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinctions in slaughtering the Hajj sacrifice (hady) based on whether it is obligatory (wajib) or voluntary (nafl), assigning Mina for the former and Makkah for the latter. It further refines the ruling by noting that animals already consecrated and adorned (ash'ara wa qallada) must be slaughtered specifically on the Day of Eid al-Adha, reflecting the precise ritual timing emphasized in Shia fiqh. This distinction highlights the importance of intent and ritual state in determining the validity and location of the sacrifice.
